local_market_longform:
Savannah is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Savannah currently trade around a median of $320,000 and take roughly 45 days to go under contract, with about 26% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Savannah runs heavily to 1800s–1920s historic homes downtown, post-war ranches, and newer coastal tracts to the west, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Savannah, the issues we see most are hurricane and coastal-flood risk, salt-air and moisture rot, termite exposure, and aging masonry and pier foundations. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like the Victorian District out to Pooler and Richmond Hill — and in Georgia the local economy anchored by the port (one of the nation's busiest), tourism, and manufacturing (Hyundai nearby) keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Chatham County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Savannah sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the Historic District squares also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Savannah. We know what a block in the Victorian District, Ardsley Park, Cuyler-Brownville, and Thomas Square actually sells for, what coastal Georgia buyers will and won't pay for, and how Chatham County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Savannah house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Georgia title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Savannah pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Savannah homes in any condition — including the hurricane and coastal-flood risk we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Savannah neighborhood — places like the Victorian District — the home's condition, and current coastal Georgia demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Georgia?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Georgia permits direct purchases; we market our own equitable interest and disclose our role in writing.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Chatham County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
